tool_input.message:
Reopening — a real defect, and partly my fault for accepting a bad characterization.

The operator opened the PDF and found Z content **running off the right edge of the page and being cut off**. The prose writer had reported the overfull-hbox warnings as "cosmetic only," I accepted that without rendering a page, and it is wrong: predicate text is genuinely truncated mid-expression.

**My detection method was also wrong, which is why I underestimated it.** I grepped the log for `Overfull \hbox (...) in paragraph at lines` — but Z schemas are alignments, so their overflows are reported as **`in alignment at lines`**. I missed every severe one. Use both patterns:

```
grep -oE "Overfull \\\\hbox \([0-9.]+pt too wide\) in (paragraph|alignment) at lines [0-9]+--[0-9]+" architecture.log
```

**The five Z overflows, worst first:**

| too wide | schema | line |
|---|---|---|
| **468.5pt** | `VerifyCommandSignature` | 988 |
| 247.2pt | `ResolveCredential` | 365 |
| 177.8pt | `ClassifyTrust` | 249 |
| 120.3pt | `DaemonGate` | 1066 |
| 38.4pt | the given-types `zed` | 169 |

468pt is roughly a full text-width overrun — your eight-case schema is the worst affected, and it is the one whose exhaustiveness argument a reader most needs to be able to follow.

**Root cause:** a newline in the *source* inside a schema predicate does not produce a rendered line break. Only `\\` does. So continuation lines that look wrapped in the source typeset as one very long line.

**Technique — and note this, because the obvious answer does not work here.** The operator suggested `\t1`, which is fuzz's tab macro (`\def\t#1{\afterassignment\@t\count@=#1}`, `\zedtab = 2em`). I tested it: **`\t1` fails in this document.** Something reloads the LaTeX kernel's `\t` tie-accent after `fuzz.sty`, so `\t1` errors with `! Please use \mathaccent for accents in math mode` and the build dies. Do not use it.

**`\quad` works.** I verified end to end on a scratch copy of `ResolveCredential`: `fuzz` exit 0, `latexmk` exit 0, and that schema's 247pt overflow disappeared. Pattern:

```latex
  (keychainAvail = ztrue \land name? \in \dom keychainValues \\
  \quad \implies value! = keychainValues(name?)) \\
  \land \\
  ((\lnot (keychainAvail = ztrue \land name? \in \dom keychainValues)) \\
  \quad \land name? \in \dom fileValues \\
  \quad \implies value! = fileValues(name?)) \\
```

Use `\qquad` for a second level where a conjunct nests.

**Please fix all five.** Break at operator boundaries — before `\implies`, before `\land`, before `\lor` — so the logical structure stays readable rather than wrapping arbitrarily. For `VerifyCommandSignature` specifically, each of the eight cases should read as its own visually distinct block; that schema's value is that a reader can check the case split by eye, and right now they cannot.

There are also ~14 prose overfulls, worst 53.9pt at lines 1148--1155 and 51.1pt at 113--133. Lower priority than the Z, but fix any that visibly truncate.

**Verify:** `fuzz -t` exit 0; `latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error` exit 0; then re-run the corrected grep and report the before/after overfull counts. Baseline is 19 total. Also confirm the page count — if it changes materially, say so.

Commit, do not push. And note the general lesson for the report: `fuzz` proved the Z was well-typed and `latexmk` exited 0, and the document was still unreadable on the page. Neither gate checks whether output fits.
